newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ORIOLES AGREE ON TWO-YEAR EXTENSION FOR RIPKEN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ORIOLES AGREE ON TWO-YEAR EXTENSION FOR RIPKEN.

text.p: Ironman Cal Ripken will have to wait a few more years before his guaranteed first-ballot entry into the Baseball Hall of Fame after agreeing on a two-year contract extension with the Baltimore Orioles, the team announced Wednesday.
The agreement was announced after Ripken hit a home run and two doubles to lead the Orioles past Kansas City, 4-2, in the season opener for both teams.
"I don't think we had a deal until after the home run," Ripken joked.
Ripken, who will play third base for the Orioles this year after 16 seasons at shorstop, would have been a free agent at the end of the year.

He will now remain an Oriole through 1999 and the team has an option for the 2000 season, when Ripken will be 39 years old and his consecutive games played streak will be at 2,802, barring injury or rest.
"I work hard and I've always wanted to be an Oriole. This is a very happy day," Ripken said.
Ripken agreed to move to third base after playing all but eight of his record-setting 2,316 consecutive games at short.
He is the club's all-time leader in homers (353), RBI (1,369), doubles (487) and runs (1,366) and is second in hits (2,549) and games (2,381).
